svg.title: Asynchronous Request-Reply
svg.desc: Asynchronous Request-Reply. Accept now with 202, process in the background, and let the client poll a status URL. Step 1, A long synchronous call: The report takes ~2 min, but the gateway cuts the call at 30 s; the retry renders it a second time. Step 2, Accept now, work later: The API saves job 42, queues it and answers 202 at once, with Location: /jobs/42 and Retry-After. Step 3, Poll the status: The client polls /jobs/42 every 5 s; once the report is ready, 303 See Other points to /reports/42. Step 4, Make it robust: With the same Idempotency-Key the retry gets job 43 back, not a second job. DELETE cancels it.

g.text: The report takes ~2 min, but the gateway cuts the call at 30 s; the retry renders it a second time.
The API saves job 42, queues it and answers 202 at once, with Location: /jobs/42 and Retry-After.
The client polls /jobs/42 every 5 s; once the report is ready, 303 See Other points to /reports/42.
With the same Idempotency-Key the retry gets job 43 back, not a second job. DELETE cancels it.
If the client can take calls,
a webhook can tell it instead.
Still no report, and the API
with a GET at the Location.
✕ the 202 is lost on the way
the same job, not a second one
The answer is the PDF itself,
so the call stays open until
Each copy burns CPU and memory
a poll never waits for the work.
No client has to poll forever.
each row is deleted 24 h after its job ends
the worker writes it, the API reads it
